Let \(X\) be the set of \(k\)-subsets of \([n]\), and let \(A\) be the adjacency matrix of \(KG(n,k)\).

Since \(n\ge 3k-1\), if \(S,T\in X\) intersect and \(S\ne T\), then
\[
|[n]\setminus(S\cup T)|=n-|S\cup T|\ge n-(2k-1)\ge k,
\]
so there exists a \(k\)-set disjoint from both \(S\) and \(T\). Hence
\[
d(S,T)=
\begin{cases}
0,&S=T,\\
1,&S\cap T=\varnothing,\\
2,&S\ne T,\ S\cap T\ne\varnothing.
\end{cases}
\]
Thus, writing \(q=2^p\),
\[
D_p=(d(S,T)^p)_{S,T}=A+q(J-I-A)=q(J-I)+(1-q)A.
\]
On the zero-sum subspace \(J=0\), so the relevant operator is
\[
-qI+(1-q)A.
\]

The Kneser adjacency eigenvalues are
\[
\lambda_j=(-1)^j\binom{n-k-j}{k-j},\qquad j=0,1,\dots,k,
\]
with multiplicity
\[
m_j=\binom nj-\binom n{j-1}.
\]
For completeness, these come from the filtration spanned by indicators of \(k\)-sets containing a fixed \(j\)-set: modulo the previous level, \(A\) acts by
\[
(-1)^j\binom{n-k-j}{k-j}.
\]

Therefore the eigenvalue of \(D_p\) on the \(j\)-th nonconstant eigenspace is
\[
\mu_j(p)=\lambda_j-q(1+\lambda_j).
\]
If \(j\) is even, \(\lambda_j>0\), so \(\mu_j(p)<0\) for all \(q>1\). If \(j\) is odd, write
\[
b_j=\binom{n-k-j}{k-j},
\]
so \(\lambda_j=-b_j\). Then
\[
\mu_j(p)=q(b_j-1)-b_j.
\]
Thus we need
\[
q\le \frac{b_j}{b_j-1}
\]
for every odd \(j\) with \(b_j>1\).

The numbers \(b_j\) strictly decrease with \(j\), since
\[
\frac{b_j}{b_{j+1}}=\frac{n-k-j}{k-j}>1
\]
for \(j<k\). Hence the strongest condition is at \(j=1\). Put
\[
B=\binom{n-k-1}{k-1}.
\]
Then
\[
2^p\le \frac{B}{B-1},
\]
so
\[
\wp=\log_2\!\left(\frac{B}{B-1}\right).
\]

At \(p=\wp\), equality occurs only for \(j=1\), because \(b_j\) is strictly decreasing. Therefore \(E\) is exactly the first nonconstant eigenspace, whose dimension is
\[
m_1=\binom n1-\binom n0=n-1.
\]

\[
\boxed{\left(\log_2\!\left(\frac{\binom{n-k-1}{k-1}}{\binom{n-k-1}{k-1}-1}\right),\ n-1\right)}
\]
